answer.headline: Commercial airports in high-income CBSAs, ranked by average seats per departure
answer.body:
Commercial airports are the US airports at or above the catalog enplanement floor. An airport is in the ranked set when its calculated home-CBSA per-capita income in {F177.period} is above the per-capita-income cutoff named in the question. None of the returned incomes for that commercial set sat on the cutoff itself. The ranking metric is calculated average seats per departure over {F371.period}, with higher gauge placed first. These values are calculated. The order is a gauge ranking, not the investment screening model and not a valuation.

SFO {F316}, OAK {F249}, and CCR {F67} repeat the same home-CBSA per-capita income. Shared-CBSA income is an area figure and is not additive. The same repetition applies wherever airports in the list share a home CBSA.

DIK {F396}, EAR {F398}, and PIR {F438} are tied on calculated gauge. Their relative order in the list is not a measured difference. Displayed gauges elsewhere can look equal after rounding even when the calculated values differ. The list order follows the unrounded calculated gauge.

claims.text: Each ranked airport has calculated home-CBSA per-capita income in {F177.period} above the cutoff named in the question.
The list orders those airports by calculated average seats per departure over {F371.period}, from AFW at {F371} to MRI at {F426}.
DIK {F396}, EAR {F398}, and PIR {F438} have the same calculated gauge, so their list order is not a measured difference.

A higher average seats per departure is a larger average aircraft gauge in this window. Using that level to evaluate aircraft upgauging describes the current gauge mix. It does not establish that gauge increased.

assumptions: Commercial airports means the catalog group at or above the enplanement floor. The words commercial airports did not resolve to a single airport or a named region.
The question names no year. Home-CBSA income uses {F177.period}, the latest calendar year covered for that metric. Average seats per departure uses the catalog T12 window {F371.period}.
Inclusion requires calculated home-CBSA per-capita income above the cutoff named in the question.
Higher average seats per departure ranks ahead of lower gauge, as the gauge reading requested for the upgauging question.
limitations: Aircraft upgauging as a change in gauge over time is not measured. No prior-window comparison or CAGR was calculated. The ranking is the level of average seats per departure.
The rank does not apply a departure-volume gate. Gauge is total seats divided by passenger departures, so a thin passenger schedule can place an airport high in the order.
Terminal capacity, unmet demand, fares, and profitability are not measured by these data.
Displayed gauge figures are rounded. Airports can show the same displayed gauge and still be ordered by different unrounded values. The exact calculated tie is DIK, EAR, and PIR.
Home-CBSA per-capita income is an area value and an administrative market-area proxy. Airports that share a CBSA repeat it. Do not add those figures across airports.

Commercial airports with no returned home-CBSA per-capita income for the income year are named in the body. The cutoff cannot be applied to them, and the reason each value is missing is not established.
This ranking is not the investment screen. It does not produce screening flags, and it is not a valuation.
